sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Hi Phil.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: Hi Georgie.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: How's your week going?

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: It's going very well, thank you.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Um, I watched a really good film last night.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: Did you watch it at home or at the cinema?

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: I watched it at home on my sofa with my housemates.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: Oh, was it good?

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: It was very good.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Uh, Now I told you I watched a film last night at home, but in this episode of Real Easy English, we're talking about cinema.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: So the cinema is where you watch films, or in American English, they're sometimes called movies.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: And before we get started, let's just um remind everyone that if you go to BBC Learning English dot com, there's a worksheet where you can practice all the language that you'll hear in this episode.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: So, Phil, do you go to the cinema often?

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: No, No, I don't go very often at all.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: What about you?

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: I don't go often, but I did go a couple of weeks ago.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: I went to see an action film, a recent action film, and it was really spectacular.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: And I'm not a big fan of action movies, action films.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: I prefer films that are a bit less stressful, um, so I wouldn't usually watch action films at home, but in the cinema it was really an amazing experience because you have the big screen, You have amazing sound, um, And I really enjoyed it.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: I've not actually been to the cinema for maybe two years, I think.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Wow, Phil, Why don't you go to the cinema?

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Do you not like it?

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: I like, I like the cinema as an event so the last time I went, I went with my kids.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: Um, I can't remember what film, but it was a big thing for them to go, and they're excited about it, but.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: I don't know.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: I, I like the big screen.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: I like the sound.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: I like the event.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: But if you want to spend time with people, I think in a cinema you can't talk to anyone.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: You sit in the dark.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: You can't talk.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: Um, And it's not the best when you want to talk to people when you want to get to know people so I tend to watch films more at home to be honest.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Yeah but what about if you go to the cinema with people that you see very often and you don't need to catch up or find out about their lives You're just going to watch a film and to relax.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: Yeah I mean yeah that makes sense because it is it is it is nice to get out It is nice to get out of the house and see it on a big screen.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: There are also other downsides to going to the cinema.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: My big thing with the cinema is that the seats are not very comfortable.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: It's much more comfortable to watch a film at home because you might have a sofa, blankets, you can lie down, You don't have to sit like we are now in a chair, upright.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Yeah, it's really nice at home.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: You have your snacks.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: You don't have to pay for them as well.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: I also think TVs that people have at home now are much better than they used to be.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: When I was a kid, you had a tiny little TV and it was so different to watching something at the cinema.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: But now I've got quite a nice telly.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: So Phil, you talked about going to the cinema as like an event.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: So something we do for special occasions.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: I really feel that I love going to the cinema because you can buy snacks that you wouldn't normally eat, Like popcorn is something I don't eat at home, but I eat at the cinema.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: And then going in a little bit early and watching the film trailers, which are short adverts for films that are coming up soon that are shown at the cinema.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Is there anything else you like about the cinema?

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: What is nice about the cinema is that you can have no distractions You just have the film You put your phone away At least you should put your phone away Some people some people in the cinema don't follow the rules but hopefully everyone watching puts their phone away There's no distractions You can just relax and get involved in the film.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: It's really nice.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: It is really annoying when people in front of you or next to you are talking really loudly throughout the film.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: It's okay to whisper, So that's when you whisper like that.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: It's okay to do that every now and again, but if they're talking all the way through the film, that is really annoying.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: Yeah.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: I can't stand that.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Phil, what kind of films do you like to watch at the cinema?

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: I think a film that takes you to a different place.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: So something that's quite spectacular there's a lot happening.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: There's a lot to see.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: Or maybe a film that shows you a bit of the world that's interesting that you don't know that well.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: I kind of like films like that films that take you somewhere, that show you something you wouldn't normally see.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: That's definitely good to watch on a big screen.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Yeah, I agree.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: I wouldn't go to the cinema to watch a romantic comedy, a romcom.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: I agree with you.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: I'd like to watch something, yeah, spectacular.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Okay, Phil, it's time to look at some of the vocabulary we heard in this conversation, starting with trailers, which are short adverts for new films shown at the cinema.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: And we also talked about popcorn.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: Now, popcorn, it's a snack.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: It's made of corn, and it's usually either sweet or salty.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: Um, and it's very nice, and you get it at the cinema.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: We also heard spectacular, which is a very strong adjective to describe something that is very exciting to look at.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: And we talked about distractions, Things that are distractions, things that make you look at something you might not have wanted to look at, like someone's phone screen instead of the film.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: And the things that you watch in the cinema are called films or sometimes called movies as well okay,

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: And that's it for this week's episode of Real Easy English but don't worry, we'll be back next week with another episode in easy English.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: And don't forget to download a free worksheet to test what you've learned at bbc learning english dot com goodbye for now.

sentences.speaker: Phil
sentences.text: Bye.
